summary: The children of a father who lost his job in a layoff earn less as adults, mostly the children of low-income families.
realLife: A study of about 60,000 Canadian father and child pairs found children of displaced fathers earned about 9 percent less a year and used unemployment insurance and social assistance more often.
sources: NBER working paper w11587, The Intergenerational Effect of Worker Displacement: https://www.nber.org/papers/w11587
inGame: household income after the job-ended event; the child's school record and later job record carry the effect. needs: long-run child outcome tracking beyond the played years.
